title: Direct Preference Optimization
authors: R. Rafailov, A. Sharma, E. Mitchell, S. Ermon, C. Manning, C. Finn
before: Preference alignment meant training a reward model then running PPO against it.
problem: That pipeline is unstable, memory-hungry and hard to reproduce outside well-resourced labs.
breakthrough: Algebra showing the RL objective can be optimised directly on preference pairs, with no reward model and no RL loop.
why: It made alignment a straightforward fine-tuning job, which is why open models could align themselves at all.
next: Adopted in Llama 3's post-training and across the open ecosystem.
inherits: Preference optimisation as a simple loss rather than an RL system.
